```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
## Chunks that use the network run only when BacDive is reachable.
online <- tryCatch({
    httr2::req_perform(httr2::req_timeout(
        httr2::request("https://api.bacdive.dsmz.de/v2/fetch/24493"), 20))
    TRUE
}, error = function(e) FALSE)
## Use temporary settings, so building the vignette never changes the
## reader's own cache or settings.
options(
    bdiver.predictions = FALSE,
    bdiver.cache_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "bdiver-cache"),
    bdiver.config_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "bdiver-config")
)
```

# Introduction

[BacDive](https://bacdive.dsmz.de/), the Bacterial Diversity Metadatabase,
describes more than 100,000 bacterial and archaeal strains: their
taxonomy, morphology, physiology, growth conditions, and more. bdiver lets
you find strains, download their records, and turn them into tables, for
example for [bugphyzz](https://bioconductor.org/packages/bugphyzz).

BacDive data may only be used in compliance with the
[BacDive terms of use](https://bacdive.dsmz.de/about).

# Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("bdiver")
```

```{r load}
library(bdiver)
```

# Find strains

Each search returns the BacDive IDs of the matching strains.

```{r search, eval = online}
ids <- bdSearchTaxon("Phaeobacter", "gallaeciensis")
ids
bdSearchCultureCollection("DSM 26640")
bdSearch16S("KC176239")
bdSearchGenome("GCA_000511385")
```

# Get records

`bdFetch()` downloads the records of the strains.

```{r fetch, eval = online}
records <- bdFetch(ids)
names(records[[1]])
```

The rest of this vignette uses a record that comes with the package.

```{r example}
record <- bdExampleRecord()
record$General$description
```

# Make a table

`bdExtract()` turns records into a table with one row per strain. By
default it has the columns used by bugphyzz:

```{r default-table}
tbl <- bdExtract(list(record))
t(as.data.frame(tbl[, 1:12]))
```

To choose your own columns, give a named list. Each element is the path to
a value in the record:

```{r own-columns}
bdExtract(list(record), list(
    species = c("Name and taxonomic classification", "species"),
    gram_stain = c("Morphology", "cell morphology", "gram stain"),
    medium = c("Culture and growth conditions", "culture medium", "name")
))
```

You can also start from the default columns and change them:

```{r change-defaults}
columns <- bdDefaultFields()
columns$colony_color <- NULL
columns$keywords <- c("General", "keywords")
```

The table is a `DataFrame` from `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("S4Vectors")`. It
works like a `data.frame`, and also records where each column comes from
and which BacDive release the data are from:

```{r dataframe}
S4Vectors::mcols(tbl)[1:4, ]
S4Vectors::metadata(tbl)$release
```

# Export to a file

`bdExport()` writes records to a file, one row per strain:

```{r export, eval = online}
out <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
bdExport(out, ids = ids)
read.csv(out)[, 1:4]
```

Without `ids`, it exports all of BacDive. This takes about an hour; if it
is interrupted, run the same call again and it continues where it stopped.

```{r export-all, eval = FALSE}
bdExport("bacdive.csv")
```

# Cache

bdiver can save downloaded records so they are not downloaded again. The
first time you download data, it asks whether to use the cache. You can
also turn it on or off yourself:

```{r cache-enable}
bdCacheEnable()
```

With the cache, records from several searches can be combined without
downloading any strain twice:

```{r cache-example, eval = online}
ids <- c(bdSearchTaxon("Phaeobacter"), bdSearchTaxon("Ruegeria"))
tbl <- bdExtract(bdFetch(ids))
dim(tbl)
```

`bdCacheInfo()` describes the cache, and `bdCacheClear()` deletes it.
When BacDive publishes a new release, bdiver tells you, and you can clear
the cache to download the new data.

```{r cache-info, eval = online}
bdCacheInfo()
bdCacheClear(ask = FALSE)
```

# AI-predicted traits

BacDive also predicts some traits, such as Gram stain or motility, from
genome sequences. bdiver includes these predictions only if you ask, with
`predictions = TRUE` or with `bdPredictionsEnable()`. They are kept in
separate columns from observed values:

```{r predictions}
t(as.data.frame(bdExtract(list(record), bdPredictionFields("motility"))))
```

`bdSettings()` shows whether the cache and predictions are turned on:

```{r settings}
bdSettings()
```

# Session information

```{r session}
sessionInfo()
```
